h3. Environment

QA branch https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders — API host sv8785api.qa.shopview.com — build marker <meta name="app-version"> = v3.4.2-4f8211c (index.html last-modified Mon, 03 Aug 2026 20:09:32 GMT) — observed 2026-08-04, org d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f, location "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919", signed in as an Administrator.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Open Work Orders on a desktop browser at a 1680x1050 window, on the All tab.
# Look at where the five filter buttons (Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on Site) sit in relation to the tab row (All, Estimates, Completed, My Work Orders).
# Click the filter icon to the left of the Status button to collapse the filter bar.
# Watch whether the table moves up into the space the buttons were using.

h3. Expected Result

The five filter buttons sit on their own row directly BELOW the tab row, and when the bar is collapsed the table moves up and uses the space that is freed.

h3. Current Result

The filter buttons sit on the SAME row as the tabs, to the right of "My Work Orders". Because they share the tab row there is no separate row to give back: collapsing hides the buttons but the table does not move up at all. The table header stays in exactly the same place before and after collapsing.

h3. How often

Every time, on desktop.

h3. Technical detail

Measured from the DOM: the tab elements are at y=85 with height 40; the five buttons (CSS class "filter-chip") are at y=90 with height 30 and x from 452 to 1164, i.e. inside the same band, to the right of the tabs. The table head element stays at y=144 both before and after clicking the collapse toggle (data-test-id="toggle_filter_bar"). The approved design frame for the final desktop layout (Figma node 11854:24657) also draws the bar on its own row below the tabs.

h3. Environment

QA branch https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders 

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Open Work Orders on desktop, All tab, with no filters and nothing typed in the page Search.
# Click the "Search" button in the page toolbar (to the left of the columns icon) and type: Lastone

Observe: 
The Page wont filter the results with Lastone.


h3. Expected Result

The page should show the data related to Lastone only.


h3. Current Result

Page search is not working.

h3. 

!image-20260805-024810.png|width=921,alt="image-20260805-024810.png"!

[^screen-capture - 2026-08-05T074453.985.webm]

 

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Filters specification, version 18, requirement S13-R7, which says: "The query applies as the user types, debounced at 300ms. There is no apply or submit button and Enter is not required."

And requirement S13-R12, which says: "Results replace the table contents in place. There is no separate results view or results page." Together those two mean that typing into the page search must narrow the list on the page itself.

h3. Environment

QA branch https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders — API host sv8785api.qa.shopview.com — build marker <meta name="app-version"> = v3.4.2-4f8211c (index.html last-modified Mon, 03 Aug 2026 20:09:32 GMT) — observed 2026-08-04, org d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f, location "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919", signed in as an Administrator.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Open Work Orders on desktop, All tab, with no filters and nothing typed in the page Search.
# Click the "Search" button in the page toolbar (to the left of the columns icon) and type: Lastone
# Check that the list narrows to the two Lastone Construction work orders S2-9473 and S2-9120.
# Now type something that matches nothing, for example: ZZQQNOMATCHXX
# Close the browser completely (not just the tab) and open it again, sign in, and go to Work Orders.

h3. Expected Result

What you typed in the page search belongs to that browser tab only. When you come back later the search box is empty and you see the normal, unsearched list of work orders.

h3. Current Result

The text you typed is saved against your user account. When you come back later the page re-applies it by itself: the address bar becomes .../workorders?search=ZZQQNOMATCHXX and the list shows NO work orders at all. A user who does not notice the search box will believe their work orders have disappeared.

h3. How often

Every time.

h3. Technical detail

Typing in the page search fires PUT /api/users/me/preferences/work-orders-list with the query inside the saved value, e.g. {"value":{"tab":"estimate","filters":{},"collapsed":false,"columns":{...},"sortBy":"companyName","descending":true,"search":"Lastone"}} and the following GET returns it. Verified in a brand-new browser context with empty localStorage and sessionStorage, which restored search=ZZQQNOMATCHXX and rendered zero rows. The specification is explicit that the query must never be stored against the account: S10-R5, S13-R25 and S13-N4.

h3. Environment

QA branch https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders 

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# On a phone (or a browser window 390 pixels wide), sign in and open this address: https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders?status=declined&tab=all
# Look at the filter buttons above the list.
# Look at the status shown on the work order cards below them.

h3. Expected Result

The page opens with the Declined filter already applied and the cards below show only Declined work orders, exactly as it does on a desktop screen.

h3. Current Result

The filter buttons say filters are on — "All Filters (1)" and "Status (1)" are both highlighted in blue — but the cards listed are all Estimate work orders for the customer Aagate Landscaping, starting with S2-15017, S2-14846 and S2-13145. 

h3. 

h3. Technical detail

With the URL above, the list request the phone sends is GET /api/work-orders?...&filters[0][field]=status&filters[0][value]=estimate&search=&showMyWorkOrders=0 — the value is "estimate", not the "declined" the URL asked for. The same happens with a second filter in the URL: the buttons read "All Filters (2)" / "Status (1)" / "Customer (1)" while the request is still status=estimate. Tapping the Status button then Paid sends filters[0][value]=paid correctly and the cards change to Paid, so the fault is specific to filter state arriving from the address bar. Specification reference S11-R2.

!image-20260805-025923.png|width=412,alt="image-20260805-025923.png"!



!image-20260805-025741.png|width=402,alt="image-20260805-025741.png"!

h3. Expected Result

The page opens with the Declined filter already applied and the cards below show only Declined work orders, exactly as it does on a desktop screen.

h3. Current Result

The filter buttons say filters are on — "All Filters (1)" and "Status (1)" are both highlighted in blue — but the cards listed are all Estimate work orders for the customer Aagate Landscaping, starting with S2-15017, S2-14846 and S2-13145. 

h3. 

h3. Technical detail

With the URL above, the list request the phone sends is GET /api/work-orders?...&filters[0][field]=status&filters[0][value]=estimate&search=&showMyWorkOrders=0 — the value is "estimate", not the "declined" the URL asked for. The same happens with a second filter in the URL: the buttons read "All Filters (2)" / "Status (1)" / "Customer (1)" while the request is still status=estimate. Tapping the Status button then Paid sends filters[0][value]=paid correctly and the cards change to Paid, so the fault is specific to filter state arriving from the address bar. Specification reference S11-R2.

!image-20260805-025923.png|width=412,alt="image-20260805-025923.png"!



!image-20260805-025741.png|width=402,alt="image-20260805-025741.png"!

 

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Filters specification, version 18, requirement S11-R2, which says: "When a user opens a URL that contains filter state, the Work Orders page loads with those filters pre-applied and the table already filtered".

That the same must hold on a phone comes from requirement S12-R2, which says: "The filter chips behave like desktop with one exception (see S12-R5): tapping a chip opens its dropdown, selections update the chip appearance, and “Clear filters” appears when active". The one exception it names is about staging selections behind an Apply button, not about which records are listed.

h3. Environment

QA branch https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders — API host sv8785api.qa.shopview.com — build marker <meta name="app-version"> = v3.4.2-4f8211c (index.html last-modified Mon, 03 Aug 2026 20:09:32 GMT) — observed 2026-08-04, org d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f, location "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919", signed in as an Administrator.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Open Work Orders on desktop, All tab, and use Clear Filters first so no filter is on.
# Click the "Search" button in the page toolbar and type text that matches nothing, for example: ZZQQNOMATCHXX
# Read the message in the empty table area and look at the link underneath it.

h3. Expected Result

The empty screen tells the user that nothing matched their search and offers a way to clear the search. Where both a search and filters are on, it offers each of them separately, so clearing one does not clear the other.

h3. Current Result

The message reads "No work orders match your filters" even though no filter is on, and the only link offered is "Clear Filters". Clicking it does nothing useful because there are no filters to clear: the search text stays and the screen stays empty. There is no way to clear the search from the empty screen.

h3. How often

Every time.

h3. Technical detail

The empty state renders one link only, data-test-id="empty_state_clear_filters", labelled "Clear Filters"; there is no clear-the-query counterpart. The toolbar copy of the same control (data-test-id="clear_filters") is hidden when no filter is active. Specification references S8-R4 and S8-R5.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Open Work Orders on desktop, All tab, and use Clear Filters first so no filter is on.
# Click the "Search" button in the page toolbar and type text that matches nothing, for example: ZZQQNOMATCHXX
# Read the message in the empty table area and look at the link underneath it.

h3. Expected Result

The empty screen tells the user that nothing matched their search and offers a way to clear the search. Where both a search and filters are on, it offers each of them separately, so clearing one does not clear the other.

h3. Current Result

The message reads "No work orders match your filters" even though no filter is on, and the only link offered is "Clear Filters". Clicking it does nothing useful because there are no filters to clear: the search text stays and the screen stays empty. There is no way to clear the search from the empty screen.

h3. How often

Every time.

h3. Technical detail

The empty state renders one link only, data-test-id="empty_state_clear_filters", labelled "Clear Filters"; there is no clear-the-query counterpart. The toolbar copy of the same control (data-test-id="clear_filters") is hidden when no filter is active. Specification references S8-R4 and S8-R5.

 

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Filters specification, version 18, and it takes three requirements, all of which the empty screen has to satisfy.

Requirement S8-R3: "When the combination of active filters and any active search query produces no matching records, the table shows an empty state with a message indicating no results were found for the current filters and search".

Requirement S8-R4: "The empty state includes a prompt or link to clear filters and, where a search query is active, to clear the query".

Requirement S8-R5: "Where both a query and filters are active, each is cleared independently from the empty state. Clearing filters does not clear the query and clearing the query does not clear the filters, consistent with S13-R13".
This work item relates to SV-8793

h3. Description

When you schedule a technician for the morning, the Schedule shows the job in the afternoon. A one-hour job put on a technician's calendar for 9:00 in the morning appears on the board, in the pop-up summary and in the shift window as 3:00 in the afternoon. Every time on the page is shifted by six hours - the block position, the hover summary, the start and end times in the shift window, and the little 'now' marker in Day view. A twelve-hour day shift that should read 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM instead reads 1:00 PM to 1:00 AM and spills over into the next day on the Day view. This makes the Schedule unusable as a planning board: nobody can tell a technician when to start, and a morning job looks like an evening job.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Week view.
# Find the work order S-15855 Vuchester Retail, unit 10123073, line ' Service - Mobile service call made by George Donald 403-369-7067' in the left-hand list (type S-15855 into 'Search work orders').
# Drag that card onto the row for technician Ayesha Khan, on the Tuesday column.
# Note that Ayesha Khan's working hours in Edit Staff Member are Monday 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Tuesday to Friday 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, so the job should start at 7:00 in the morning.
# Hover the new block and read the time range in the pop-up summary.
# Click the block and read the two time boxes in the shift window.

items.fromString:
h3. Description

When a big job is spread across several days, the Week view draws it as one labelled block on the first day with small 'continues' markers on the following days. None of those blocks can be clicked open. Nothing happens at all - no shift window, no menu. That means from the Week view a planner cannot see the detail of a spread job, cannot change its colour, cannot add a note and, most importantly, cannot delete it. The same shift opens perfectly well from the Day view and the Month view, so the information exists - it is only the Week view that will not open it.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Week view.
# Type S-14527 into 'Search work orders' to find the Qispring Rentals work order (5 lines, 40.3h estimate).
# Drag the card onto technician Brittany Anderson's row on the Monday column.
# Choose 'Schedule whole work order' and then 'Create 4 shifts'.
# Back on the Week view, click the labelled Monday block that reads 'Qispring Rentals / 5 Lines / Part of a series'.
# Click each of the small 'continues' markers on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
# Now switch to the Day view for Monday and click the same block.

h3. Expected behaviour

Clicking any part of a spread job in the Week view opens the shift window, exactly as clicking a single-day shift does, so the planner can see the detail, recolour it, add a note or delete it.

h3. Current behaviour

In the Week view neither the labelled block nor any 'continues' marker responds to a click - no window opens. Right-clicking and double-clicking do nothing either. The very same shift opens normally from the Day view and the Month view.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

Verified by clicking all nine .schedule-block elements in the week in turn: the four series blocks (one schedule_series_block plus three text_schedule_series_continues) returned no .q-dialog, while the four standalone shifts and the event all opened dialog_schedule_shift_detail. In Day and Month view the same series shift opens and the dialog correctly shows 'event_repeat / Part of a series - Shift 1 of 4'. Series id 1655435d-8826-4eb6-bc4a-6dc978bdfc01.

Current behaviour

In the Week view neither the labelled block nor any 'continues' marker responds to a click - no window opens. Right-clicking and double-clicking do nothing either. The very same shift opens normally from the Day view and the Month view.

Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

Technical details for developers

Verified by clicking all nine .schedule-block elements in the week in turn: the four series blocks (one schedule_series_block plus three text_schedule_series_continues) returned no .q-dialog, while the four standalone shifts and the event all opened dialog_schedule_shift_detail. In Day and Month view the same series shift opens and the dialog correctly shows 'event_repeat / Part of a series - Shift 1 of 4'. Series id 1655435d-8826-4eb6-bc4a-6dc978bdfc01.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Schedule specification, version 23, section 4.9, which says: "Clicking a shift block opens a detail panel showing:" and then lists what the panel holds, including the scope summary, the notes and the Delete action. The specification draws no distinction between a single-day shift and one that belongs to a series, and no distinction between the day, week and month views.

items.fromString:
h3. Description

The View Options menu offers a 'Tech Hours' switch. Turning it on is supposed to show each technician's working hours next to their name, so a planner can see at a glance who starts at 6 and who starts at 8. Switching it on and off makes no visible difference anywhere on the page - not even for the one technician in this shop who actually has custom hours saved.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Week view.
# Note that technician Ayesha Khan has custom hours saved in Edit Staff Member: Monday 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Tuesday to Friday 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with Saturday and Sunday set to Not working.
# Click the View Options control in the toolbar (the sliders icon on the right).
# Note that 'Tech Hours' starts switched off, and switch it on.
# Close the menu and look at the technician names down the left-hand side, including Ayesha Khan's row.
# Switch 'Tech Hours' back off and compare - the screen is identical.

h3. Expected behaviour

With Tech Hours on, each technician's working hours appear beside their name (for example '7:00 AM - 7:00 PM' next to Ayesha Khan), and disappear again when it is switched off.

h3. Current behaviour

Nothing changes. The rows show only the initials, the name and the job title, both before and after. The number of shaded cells on the grid is also identical before, during and after (2 in every case), so no shading changes either.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

toggle_schedule_technician_hours flips its aria-checked correctly, so the control itself works and the preference is stored - nothing consumes it. A/B measured: the .fc-datagrid-cell-cushion text for the Ayesha Khan row was byte-identical ('AK Ayesha Khan') before, with the toggle on, and after; .fc-cell-shaded count 2 / 2 / 2. Spec section 9: 'Tech Hours | Off | Displays each technician's working hours next to their name.'

items.fromString:
h3. Description

When a shift clashes - a double booking, a day the technician does not work, or hours outside their shift - the shift window shows a warning banner naming the reason. The banner is supposed to carry an action that takes the planner straight to fixing it. There is no such action. The planner is told there is a problem and then left to work out for themselves how to move the job.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Week view.
# Note that technician Ayesha Khan does not work Sundays (Edit Staff Member shows Saturday and Sunday as Not working).
# Type S-15855 into 'Search work orders' to find the Vuchester Retail work order, unit 10123073, line ' Service - Mobile service call made by George Donald 403-369-7067'.
# Drag that card onto Ayesha Khan's row on a Sunday column.
# The new block gets an amber warning triangle. Click the block to open the shift window.
# Read the warning banner and look for an action next to it.

h3. Expected behaviour

The banner reads the clash reason and offers an action - an 'Adjust' button or link - that lets the planner correct the shift there and then.

h3. Current behaviour

The banner reads 'Scheduling conflict / Not a working day' and offers nothing. The only controls in the whole window are the delete bin, the close X, the colour selector, Add Note and Open Work Order.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

Enumerated every button inside dialog_schedule_shift_detail for a conflicted shift: button_shift_detail_delete, the close X, button_shift_detail_color, button_shift_detail_add_note, button_shift_detail_open_work_order. No adjust control exists under any test id or any label. Spec section 4.9: 'A conflict banner with an "Adjust" action when the shift is conflicted.'

items.fromString:
h3. Description

Two of the Schedule's confirmation windows ignore the keyboard. The 'Delete from this series?' window and the 'Reassign shift' window cannot be dismissed with Escape, and cannot be confirmed with Enter - the only way in or out of them is the mouse. Every other pop-up on the page closes with Escape, so the behaviour is inconsistent as well as inaccessible: anyone working keyboard-only gets stuck in these two windows.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Day view for a day that holds a multi-day job (use S-14527 Qispring Rentals spread over four days from a Monday).
# Click a shift in the middle of that series to open the shift window, then click the delete bin.
# The 'Delete from this series?' window opens. Press Escape - nothing happens. Press it again - still nothing. Click inside the window first and press Escape again - still nothing. Only Cancel or the close X will shut it.
# Now close everything and switch to the Week view.
# Drag any shift block from one technician's row to another technician's row.
# The 'Reassign shift' window opens asking 'Move this shift to <name> on <date>?'. Press Enter - nothing happens, the move is not confirmed. Press Escape - nothing happens either.

h3. Expected behaviour

Escape closes whichever pop-up is on top, and Enter confirms the window that is asking for confirmation, so both windows can be driven entirely from the keyboard.

h3. Current behaviour

Neither key does anything in either window. Escape does work on the shift window itself and on both toolbar menus, so it is specifically these two confirmation windows that ignore it.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

Escape tested twice on the delete-scope dialog, the second time after moving focus to a button inside it: .q-dialog count stayed 1 both times. Enter on the reassign dialog left .q-dialog count at 1 and produced no .undo-toast, so no request was sent. Escape DOES close dialog_schedule_shift_detail, schedule_view_options_menu and schedule_filter_display_menu. Spec section 7 names both windows first in its stacking order: 'Escape closes the topmost open modal or popover, following a defined stacking order (delete scope, reassign, spread, ...)' and 'Enter confirms the active confirmable dialog (delete scope, reassign, spread, event create/edit).'

items.fromString:
h3. Description

A user who has been given the Schedule but deliberately NOT given Work Orders: View still sees the complete work order list down the left of the Schedule page - customer names, unit numbers, how many lines each job has, the hours estimate and the lead technician. That is exactly the work order information their permissions were set up to keep from them. The list is supposed to be hidden for these users. This is a customer-data exposure, not a cosmetic gap: the restriction can be bypassed simply by opening the Schedule.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Go to Settings, then Roles & Permissions, and create a role that has Schedule: View switched ON and Work Orders: View switched OFF, with nothing else.
# Go to Settings, then Staff, open any active staff member and set their Role to that new role, then save.
# Sign in as that staff member.
# Open the Schedule.
# Read the left-hand panel.

h3. Expected behaviour

The left-hand panel hides the work order list for this user. They can still see the calendar and everyone's shifts, but no customer names, unit numbers, line counts, hours or lead technicians.

h3. Current behaviour

The full list is shown - 18 work order cards, each with the work order number, the customer name, the unit number, 'N lines - Xh Est.', the technician initials and the lead technician's name. Nothing is hidden.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

Reproduced with a purpose-made role holding only scheduleView (fe_permissions came back as ['scheduleView','woFullViewMode'], workOrdersView absent). The page rendered 18 sidebar_work_order_card elements. The API leaks it too: GET /api/schedule/work-orders returned HTTP 200 with the full payload for that user, so this is not only a front-end gate. For contrast the tier enforcement itself is correct: the same user got 403 on POST /api/schedule/shifts, PATCH, DELETE and POST /api/schedule/events. Spec section 14.2: 'The left panel sidebar displays work order data (customer, unit, lines, lead tech) and requires Work Orders: View to populate. If a user has Schedule access but Work Orders: View is OFF, the sidebar hides the work order list'. The probe role was deleted and the staff member restored to Technician afterwards.

fields.summary: A user who is not allowed to see work orders can still read the whole work order list on the Schedule

renderedFields.description:
Description

A user who has been given the Schedule but deliberately NOT given Work Orders: View still sees the complete work order list down the left of the Schedule page - customer names, unit numbers, how many lines each job has, the hours estimate and the lead technician. That is exactly the work order information their permissions were set up to keep from them. The list is supposed to be hidden for these users. This is a customer-data exposure, not a cosmetic gap: the restriction can be bypassed simply by opening the Schedule.

items.fromString:
h3. Description

When a big job is spread over several days, the spread window lets the planner choose how much to schedule and shows a preview - but it has no start date field. The run of days always begins on whichever day the job was dropped on, and there is no way to change it in the window. That removes the one way the planner was meant to have of making a second technician's run start AFTER the first one finishes instead of alongside it, which is how two technicians share a long job in sequence.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Week view.
# Type S-14527 into 'Search work orders' to find the Qispring Rentals work order (5 lines, 40.3h estimate).
# Drag the card onto technician Brittany Anderson's row on the Monday column and choose 'Schedule whole work order'.
# The spread window opens showing 'Brittany Anderson - Whole order - 40h 19m', a 'Schedule' choice reading 'Full estimate (40h 19m)', and a preview reading '4 shifts - 40h 19m / Aug 10 to Aug 13 - 12h/day, Mon-Thu'.
# Look for a start date field anywhere in the window.
# Try each of the other choices - 1 week, 2 weeks, 'Until a date...' and 'Specific hours...' - and look again.

h3. Expected behaviour

The spread window carries a start date that defaults to the earliest working day and can be changed, so a planner can push a second technician's run to begin after the first one ends.

h3. Current behaviour

There is no start date field in the window under any of the five choices. 'Until a date...' adds a 'Finish by' date and 'Specific hours...' adds an 'Hours per day' number, but neither lets the planner set where the run begins. The start is fixed by the cell the card was dropped on.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

Enumerated every input inside the spread dialog for all five selector values: Full estimate -> 1 text input (the selector itself); 'Until a date...' -> that plus one input[type=date] labelled 'Finish by'; 'Specific hours...' -> that plus one input[type=number] labelled 'Hours per day' pre-filled 12. No date input for the start exists in any state. The POST body confirms it: startDate is taken from the drop cell (startDate '2026-08-10'). Spec section 4.5: 'Start date. Defaults to the earliest working day. Adjusting it is how a second technician's series can be made sequential (starting after the first) rather than parallel.'

items.fromString:
h3. Description

In the Day view a planner can drag a job left or right to change what time it starts. It is meant to move in quarter-hour steps so a job can start at, say, quarter past eight. In practice the smallest move it will make is a whole hour, so anything that does not start on the hour cannot be set by dragging.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Day view for Tuesday Aug 4, 2026.
# Find any shift block on the grid - for example the Xiriver Apparel block, unit 16604, on Brittany Anderson's row.
# Note the start time in the block's hover summary.
# Press and hold the middle of the block and drag it a small distance to the right - about half of one hour column - then release.
# Read the new start time in the hover summary.

h3. Expected behaviour

The start time moves in quarter-hour steps, so a small drag moves it 15 or 30 minutes, and a job can be set to start at 8:15 or 8:45.

h3. Current behaviour

The start time jumps a whole hour. A drag of about half an hour's width moved the job a full hour, and no quarter-hour position can be reached by dragging.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

A 24-pixel drag (approximately 31 minutes at the rendered zoom) issued PATCH /api/schedule/shifts/ebdd3e03-ab10-40f3-b820-4dd7e6192892 with startsAt '2026-08-04T14:00:00.000Z', i.e. exactly +60 minutes from 13:00:00Z. Spec section 4.8: 'Horizontal drag to move a shift's start time (snaps to 15-minute intervals).' Note this is a different surface from SV-8833, which is about the start/end pickers inside the shift window; both stem from 15-minute granularity not being applied, but the drag path and the picker path are separate. The shift moved during this test was put back to 13:00:00Z afterwards.

h3. Description

The work order filters on the left of the Schedule can be switched on one at a time but not switched off in one go - there is no 'Clear all'. There is also nothing on the Filters button to show that filters are currently applied or how many, so a planner can easily be looking at a filtered list and not realise it, and then has to hunt through three groups of tick boxes to undo it.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule.
# Click 'Filters' in the left-hand panel.
# Tick 'Unassigned' under Assignment and 'Approved' under Status.
# Close the popover and note the work order list is now narrowed.
# Look at the Filters button for any badge or count showing that filters are on.
# Open the popover again and look for a 'Clear all' control.

h3. Expected behaviour

The Filters button carries a small count of how many filters are applied, and the popover has a 'Clear all' that resets every filter in one click.

h3. Current behaviour

There is no count on the button and no 'Clear all' anywhere in the popover. Each tick box has to be unticked individually.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

Enumerated the popover's contents: heading 'FILTERS' then checkbox_sidebar_assignment_unassigned / _assigned, checkbox_sidebar_status_{estimate,approved,in_progress,declined,ready_for_review,complete,invoiced,paid} and checkbox_sidebar_priority_{high,medium,low}, each with its live count. Applying a filter narrows the flat card list, and "Clear all" resets in one click.'

h3. Environment

QA branch https://sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders — build v3.4.2-d00239b (index.html last modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 22:51:02 GMT). Desktop browser, signed in as an Admin.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Open Work Orders on the All tab with no filters on.
# Click the Customer button and pick the customer named Iibay Landscaping. The button correctly reads "Customer: Iibay Landscaping" and the list narrows.
# Now leave the page and come back — any of these four does it: open a work order and click back; refresh the page; close the browser completely and sign in again; or open the same link in a new window.
# Look at the Customer button.
# Repeat the whole thing with the Lead Technician button (pick Admin ShopView) and with the Service Advisor button (pick Admin ShopView).

h3. Expected Result

The button should still read "Customer: Iibay Landscaping", the same as it did before you left the page. The user needs to see WHICH customer the list is filtered by without opening the button.

h3. Current Result

The button comes back blue (switched on) but reads only "Customer" — the customer's name is gone. The filter itself is still working: the list is still filtered by that customer, and if you open the button the name is there as a tag with a tick beside it. So the list is filtered by something the screen no longer names.

The same thing happens on the Lead Technician and Service Advisor buttons. It does NOT happen on the Status or Asset on Site buttons — those keep their value ("Status: Paid" comes back correctly), so a user sees one button naming its value and another not naming its value side by side.

h3. How often

Every time, on all four routes back to the page, on all three of those buttons. Reproduced twice from a clean start.

h3. Technical detail

The three affected filters are the ones whose choices are fetched from the server (/api/customers/list-options and the staff list); the two unaffected ones are fixed lists held in the page. On a restore the saved filter value is read back and applied to the request (filters[n][field]=company_id&filters[n][value]=00122246-ab6d-47ee-a885-3425c7bda754) but the button's label is rendered before the name for that id is available, and is not re-rendered once it arrives. Specification references: S7-R1, which says the chip "displays the selected value(s)", and S10-R1, which says filter selections are "restored exactly as they were left".

items.fromString:
h2. Description

When a manager schedules only _some_ of the jobs on a work order, the schedule offers a "Select multiple" mode with tick boxes. That mode is missing two of the controls it is supposed to have, and a third reads differently from what was asked for.

There is no *"Select all"* shortcut, so a manager who wants every job on the order has to tick each one by hand instead of pressing one button. And there is no *"Cancel"* button, so once you are in tick-box mode there is no way back to the quick single-tap list — the only way out is the small X, which throws away the whole window and you have to start again by placing the work order a second time.

It matters because picking part of a work order is the everyday case for a multi-job order, and both missing controls are the ones that make it quick and forgiving. Losing the whole window when you only wanted to step back one screen is the kind of thing that makes people avoid the feature.

h2. Branch / Environment

* Application: {{https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com}}
* API host: {{https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com}}
* Build marker ({{<meta name="app-version">}}): {{v3.5-be42149}}
* {{index.html}} last-modified: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 08:09:19 GMT
* Location / workplace: *Staging Heavy Duty - 9919*
* Observed: *2026-08-05, 14:0x UTC*

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Sign in as a user who is allowed to change the schedule (an Admin is fine) and pick the location *Staging Heavy Duty - 9919*.
# Open *Schedule* from the top navigation.
# In the left-hand panel, find work order *S-12876*, customer *Pamill Paving*, unit *713*. It has *2 lines*: *"Replace - Rear ramp handles"* (estimate 1h) and *"Quality control check over"* (no estimate). Its lead technician shows as *Brittany Anderson*. _If that work order is gone, any work order with two or more approved lines behaves the same way — the fault does not depend on which one. Proven by repeating it on the whole-order row of the same picker, which is unaffected._
# Click the small calendar button on that work order's card (its label reads *"Schedule S-12876 by click"*).
# Click an empty day cell on the row for technician *MQ Test Tech Qamar* — for example *Thursday, Aug 6*.
# The picker opens, headed *"dropped on MQ Test Tech Qamar · Thu, Aug 6"*.
# Click *"Select multiple"*.
# Tick one line, for example *"Replace - Rear ramp handles"*.
# Look along the bottom bar of the picker, and look for a way to go back to the ordinary single-tap list.

h2. Expected behaviour

In tick-box mode the bottom bar should offer a running tally, a *"Select all"* shortcut that is the same as choosing the whole work order, and a *"Cancel"* that returns you to the quick single-tap list.

The Schedule specification asks for exactly that:

{quote}"'Select multiple' is an opt-in control that switches the line rows into checkboxes and shows a confirm bar with a running tally ("Create shift · 2 lines · 6h"), a "Select all" shortcut (equivalent to whole order), and Cancel (returns to the fast single-tap list)."{quote}

h2. Current behaviour

* The tick boxes appear correctly, one per line.
* The bottom bar shows a tally, but it reads *"1 selected · 1h"* rather than the "Create shift · 2 lines · 6h" shape the specification gives.
* The confirm button reads *"Schedule"*.
* *There is no "Select all" button anywhere in the picker.* The only "All" control is the *"All 2"* chip higher up, which is the filter that switches between all lines and unscheduled lines — it does not tick anything.
* *There is no "Cancel" button.* The only way out is the *X* in the top corner, which closes the whole picker rather than returning to the single-tap list.

h2. Images

No screenshot is attached. The finding was taken by reading the picker's own rendered text and its controls directly from the running page, and the exact strings are reproduced above and in the technical section, so an image would add nothing a reader cannot already check by following the steps.

h2. Technical details for developers

Observed in the live DOM with the picker open in multi-select mode.

Controls present inside the picker ({{data-test-id}}):

{noformat}text_line_picker_dropped_on      button_line_picker_close
text_line_picker_title           line_picker_whole_work_order
button_line_picker_multi_select  input_line_picker_search

h2. Description

When a manager schedules only _some_ of the jobs on a work order, the schedule offers a "Select multiple" mode with tick boxes. That mode is missing two of the controls it is supposed to have, and a third reads differently from what was asked for.

There is no *"Select all"* shortcut, so a manager who wants every job on the order has to tick each one by hand instead of pressing one button. And there is no *"Cancel"* button, so once you are in tick-box mode there is no way back to the quick single-tap list — the only way out is the small X, which throws away the whole window and you have to start again by placing the work order a second time.

It matters because picking part of a work order is the everyday case for a multi-job order, and both missing controls are the ones that make it quick and forgiving. Losing the whole window when you only wanted to step back one screen is the kind of thing that makes people avoid the feature.

h3. Type of Issue

Defect against the build — on a phone the page search control is absent, and the toolbar search button opens the global search instead, which does not narrow the list.

h3. Environment

QA branch — sv8785.qa.shopview.com/workorders. Build v3.4.2-d00239b (index.html last-modified Tue 04 Aug 2026 22:51:02 GMT). Mobile viewport 390 x 844, touch enabled, iPhone user agent. Signed in as Admin ShopView, Administrator, workplace Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Open the Work Orders page on a phone-sized viewport (390 x 844).
# Look at the action row. There is one search control, the magnifier button.
# Tap it.
# Type a customer name that exists in the list — use Bahampton Holdings.
# Watch the work order list and the address bar.

h3. Actual Result

* There is no page search control on mobile at all. The only search element in the action row is the magnifier button, and tapping it opens the GLOBAL search — the input that appears is the global search field, accompanied by a global-search close button.
* Typing Bahampton into it does not narrow the list. The list stays at 30 work orders, the address bar stays at /workorders?tab=all with no search parameter, and no list request carrying a search term is sent.
* The primary call to action, Create Work Order, keeps a width of 332px on a 390px-wide viewport. It does not fall back to its natural hug width, so there is no free space in the action row for a search field to expand into.

h3. Expected Result

S13-R17: "On mobile the expanded field fills the remaining width of the action row rather than taking the fixed 180px desktop width. On Work Orders that resolves to 162px. All other toolbar actions remain visible and in position throughout".

S13-R18: "To create that room, the primary CTA on mobile uses its natural hug width instead of stretching to fill the row: 'New Work Order' is 144px, the same width it has on desktop, not 211px."

So on a phone the page search should expand inline in the action row to roughly 162px and narrow the work order list as the user types, exactly as it does on desktop, while the primary call to action shrinks to its hug width to make room. The global search is a separate control and must not stand in for it — the specification keeps them distinct, and the global search does not filter a page list.

h3. Test Data

* Customer searched for: Bahampton Holdings — it has 6 work orders, so a working page search would visibly narrow the list to those 6.
* The same search term typed into the DESKTOP page search on the same build does narrow the list correctly to 7 rows showing only Bahampton Holdings, which is what makes the mobile behaviour a phone-specific gap rather than a broken search.
* Values tried and ruled out: the term is not the problem (it works on desktop); no page_search_toggle element exists anywhere in the mobile document, so this is not a matter of the control being collapsed or scrolled out of view.

h3. Technical Notes

* On desktop the control is the element carrying data-test-id page_search_toggle, which expands into page_search_input. Neither element is present in the document on a mobile viewport.
* The mobile magnifier button carries data-test-id button_open_mobile_search, and what it opens is the element carrying data-test-id select_global_search, together with button_global_search_close.
* Measured on the build: Create Work Order 332px against a 390px viewport.

content.text: Withdrawing this ticket - it was raised in error.

This was reported by us. It says the Business Hours switch shades nothing in Day view. That is not right, and the reason is our own mistake: the test case it came from starts with a precondition that says
"The shop has working hours set"

, and when we looked at the screen the shop had no business hours set at all. The switch on the location screen was off, so there were no opening or closing times for the schedule to work from. With nothing set, there are no out-of-hours to shade, so shading nothing was the correct thing for it to do.
Re-checked today with the shop's hours actually set, and it works correctly.
The shop hours were set to 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, and the same Day view was looked at again on build v3.5-7ec992f:
With Business Hours turned OFF, nothing is shaded at all.
With it turned ON, two shaded bands appear - one covering midnight to 6 AM, and one covering 6 PM to midnight. The working day itself, 6 AM to 6 PM, is left clear.
Turning it off again removes the shading. This was repeated and behaved the same way each time.
The shaded band starts at exactly the 6 PM mark on the timeline, which is the shop's closing time, so it is shading the right hours and not simply shading something.
The test case behind this now passes, so nothing needs to be fixed.
Closing this rather than deleting it, so the reasoning stays on the record for anyone who looks at it later.
Description

The Schedule has a display switch called Business Hours. It is meant to grey out the parts of the day the shop is not open, so that a planner can see at a glance which part of the row is real working time and which part is the middle of the night.

The switch does nothing you can see. With it turned on, the whole timeline from midnight through to eleven at night is the same flat white as the working day, so a shift placed at three in the morning looks exactly as normal as one placed at ten in the morning.

It matters because this is the only cue on the board that tells a planner where the working day begins and ends. Without it, out-of-hours work is invisible until somebody notices the time and questions it, and the switch itself looks broken because turning it on and off changes nothing on screen.
Branch / Environment
Application: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com
API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com
Build marker (<meta name="app-version">): v3.5-7ec992f
index.html last-modified: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT, etag e2a80a6ab5e0b47c29fd88af9db1e980
Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f
Location / workplace: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton)
Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator)
Observed: 2026-08-06, 03:0x UTC
Steps to reproduce
Sign in as a user who can view the schedule (an Administrator is fine) and pick the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
Open Schedule from the top navigation.

Switch to Day view using the Day / Week / Month control, and go to Thursday, 6 August 2026. Any day behaves the same way; the fault does not depend on the date or on any particular work order, technician or shift, and no test data is needed to see it.
Open the FILTER & DISPLAY dropdown in the toolbar and find the Business Hours switch. It is already on, which is its default.
Look along the timeline from 12 AM through to 11 PM.
Turn the Business Hours switch off, look again, then turn it back on and look a third time.
Expected behaviour
With the switch on, the hours outside the working day should be covered by a grey overlay so they are visibly different from the working part of the day.
The Schedule specification asks for exactly that, in two places:
"With the toggle on, the hours OUTSIDE the working day are shaded with a grey overlay."
Governing requirement: Schedule specification, Confluence page 713031682, version 23, section 9 (Business Hours) and section 4.8 (Business-hours shading).
Current behaviour
With the switch ON, the timeline from 12 AM to 11 PM renders uniformly white. Nothing is shaded, tinted or bordered.
With the switch OFF, the timeline looks identical.
With the switch turned back ON, the timeline still looks identical.
The only shaded element anywhere in the calendar in all three states is the divider between the department groups, which is unrelated to the time of day.
Images

No screenshot is attached. The finding was taken by reading the rendered page directly and was confirmed on a screen capture at the time, and the check is a single glance at the timeline, so an image adds nothing a reader cannot see immediately by following the steps.
Technical details for developers
Measured with the toggle ON, OFF and restored to ON. In each of the three states the count of elements carrying the shaded cell class was the same:

Elements matching fc-cell-shaded: 2 in all three states. Both are the resource-timeline divider (class fc-resource-timeline-divider fc-cell-shaded), which separates the department groups; neither is a time-of-day overlay.
No element in the Day-view time grid carries any non-working-hours class, background tint or overlay in any of the three states.
Confirmed visually on the captured screenshot, not only by class name.
This is not the same as the two nearby reports, and a duplicate search was run before filing:
SV-8827 is about the switch's DEFAULT STATE (it starts on when it should start off). This report is about the switch having no visible effect at all, whichever way it is set.
SV-8837 and SV-8915 are about where the view is scrolled to when it opens. This report is about the shading of the hours once you are looking at them.

items.fromString:
h3. Description

When a job is waiting in the Unassigned row and somebody drags it onto a technician, the job moves to that technician correctly - but its start time is silently changed to six hours earlier than it was.

In the case observed, the job was booked for 7:00 in the morning while it sat unassigned. After it was dragged onto a technician, the saved start time became 1:00 in the morning. Nobody asked for that and nothing on screen warned about it. The technician it was given to starts at 7:00am, so the job was moved to a time she is not even at work.

This is worth separating from the display problem already reported in SV-8848. There, the times are stored correctly and shown wrongly. Here, the stored value itself is changed by the act of assigning, so the record is wrong from that moment on - and it would stay wrong even after the display problem is fixed. The two are very likely the same underlying time-zone handling, once on the way in and once on the way out.

It matters because it quietly corrupts real data. A planner books the morning, hands the job to a technician, and the schedule now says the small hours - which is both wrong and outside that technician's working hours, so it will also raise a conflict warning that has no real cause.

h3. Branch / Environment

* Application: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com
* API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com
* Build marker (<meta name="app-version">): v3.5-7ec992f
* index.html last-modified: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT, etag e2a80a6ab5e0b47c29fd88af9db1e980
* Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f
* Location / workplace: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton)
* Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator)
* Observed: 2026-08-06, 02:5x UTC

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Sign in as a user who is allowed to change the schedule (an Administrator is fine) and pick the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
# Open Schedule from the top navigation and go to the week containing Saturday, 8 August 2026.
# Find a job sitting in the Unassigned row. The one used here was work order S-12876, customer Pamill Paving, unit 713, line "Replace - Rear ramp handles", sitting unassigned on Sat, Aug 8. The Unassigned row sits BELOW every technician row and you have to scroll down to reach it; it is only drawn in a date range that already contains an unassigned job, so if you cannot see it, place one there first by dragging a work order onto it.
# Open the job and note its start time. This one read 7:00 AM local (stored as 2026-08-08T13:00:00Z).
# Drag that block up onto a technician's row for the same day. The technician used here was Kellie Ayers (Foreman), whose configured working hours are 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.
# Confirm the "Move this shift to Kellie Ayers on Sat, Aug 8?" dialog with Reassign.
# Open the job again and read its start time.

h3. Expected behaviour

Assigning an unassigned job to a technician should move it to that technician and leave its start time exactly as it was.

The Schedule specification asks for exactly that:

_"Dragging an unassigned shift onto a technician row assigns it to that technician."_

Governing requirement: Schedule specification, Confluence page 713031682, version 23, sections 3.2 (Unassigned placeholder) and 4.2.

h3. Current behaviour

* The job does move to the chosen technician, and it does leave the Unassigned row. That part is correct.
* The technician is correctly added to the work-order line's technician list - it went from 8 names to 9, with all 8 previous names kept.
* But the saved start time moves six hours earlier. It went from 2026-08-08T13:00:00Z (7:00 AM local) to 2026-08-08T07:00:00Z (1:00 AM local).
* 1:00 AM is outside the receiving technician's own working hours of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.

What was tried and ruled out:

* It is not a display artefact. The value quoted above is the stored value read back from the record itself after the move, not a time read off the board.
* It is not the technician's hours being applied. Her configured start is 7:00 AM, and 7:00 AM is exactly the number that ended up stored - but stored as 7:00 UTC rather than 7:00 local. The right number was written into the wrong time frame.
* It is not the drag path. The same block dragged between two technician rows opens the same confirmation dialog and completes normally.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The fault is in the saved value rather than in anything drawn on screen, so a picture of the board would not show it; the before and after values are quoted in full above and in the technical section.

h3. Technical details for developers

* Before the move: startsAt 2026-08-08T13:00:00Z, ends 14:00Z, technician Unassigned. The shift window showed 13:00 to 14:00.
* After the move: staffId 776696c4-5351-4fcc-a27b-99cdbfe2cacf (Kellie Ayers), startsAt 2026-08-08T07:00:00Z - a six-hour backward shift of the stored instant.
* Location time zone is America/Edmonton, which is UTC-6 on that date. 13:00Z is 07:00 local; 07:00Z is 01:00 local.
* Kellie Ayers' configured working window is 420 to 1140 minutes, i.e. 07:00 to 19:00 local.
* The confirmation dialog read "Reassign shift | S-12876 - Pamill Paving | Move this shift to Kellie Ayers on Sat, Aug 8?" and the toast read "Shift reassigned. Undo".
* Work order S-12876 is 582a8993-793d-4e6f-8dd0-abec5b4a3be0; the line used is "Replace - Rear ramp handles".

Relationship to SV-8848: that report covers times being SHOWN six hours later than they were scheduled. This one covers the stored value being WRITTEN six hours earlier when a job is assigned. Same six hours, opposite direction, opposite side of the boundary - most likely one missing time-zone conversion applied on read and another on write. Fixing the display alone would leave records already damaged by this path still wrong.

items.fromString:
h3. Description

A staff member's working hours cannot be opened at all if that person belongs to a different location from the one you are currently working in. The Staff list shows everyone in the organisation, so you can find the person, open them, and switch on *Set custom hours for this technician* — and at that point the screen gives up with an error and switches the toggle back off. There is no way to reach their hours from the location you are in.

It matters because the Schedule uses each technician's working hours for the start time of a new shift, for the before-hours and after-hours conflict warnings and for the capacity bars. A shop that runs two locations cannot set those hours for anyone outside whichever location they happen to be viewing, and the screen gives no hint that switching location is what is needed — it simply looks broken.

This affects a substantial part of the staff list rather than one unlucky record: of the 161 people in the list, 63 cannot have their hours opened from the Heavy Duty location and 98 can.

h3. Branch / Environment

* Application: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com
* API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com
* Build marker ({{<meta name="app-version">}}): {{v3.5-7ec992f}}
* index.html last-modified: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT, etag {{e2a80a6ab5e0b47c29fd88af9db1e980}}
* Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f
* Location / workplace while reproducing: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton)
* Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator)
* Observed: 2026-08-06, 05:0x UTC

h3. Steps to reproduce

The exact test data is named below so that the result does not depend on which person is picked — the behaviour follows the person's location, not the person.

# Sign in as an Administrator and make sure the location selected at the top of the app is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
# Go to Administration and open the Staff list.
# Find *Benjamin Peters*. His record belongs to the other location, *Staging Lethbridge - 4310*, but he is listed here all the same.
# Open his record with the edit (pencil) icon on his row.
# Switch on *Set custom hours for this technician*.
# Now change the location at the top of the app to *Staging Lethbridge - 4310*, open the same person again and switch the same toggle on.

For a direct contrast in the same sitting, repeat steps 3 to 5 with *Ayesha Khan AK*, who belongs to Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Her hours open normally, which shows the editor itself is working.

h3. Expected behaviour

Switching the toggle on should reveal the Monday-to-Sunday From/To editor and let the hours be set, for any staff member the Staff list offers.

The Schedule specification describes the technician working-hours editor without any condition about which location the person is being viewed from:

{{"Set custom hours for this technician" reveals a per-day (Mon-Sun) From/To editor for that technician.}}

Governing requirement: Schedule specification, Confluence page 713031682, version 23, section 4.2 (Working Hours).

If the hours genuinely are meant to be per-location, then the expected behaviour is that the screen says so — either by not offering the toggle, or by telling the user which location they need to switch to. What should not happen is an error that reads as a fault.

h3. Current behaviour

* The toggle flicks on and then immediately back to off, and this inline error appears: {{Couldn't load this technician's hours, so they can't be edited right now. Close and reopen the dialog to try again.}}
* Closing and reopening the dialog, as the message suggests, makes no difference. It fails the same way every time.
* No editor is ever shown, so the hours cannot be set at all from this location.
* Changing the location to Staging Lethbridge - 4310 and repeating the same steps on the same person *works immediately*: the editor appears and the hours can be edited.
* Changing the location back to Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 brings the failure back.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The visible symptom is a single line of error text quoted above, and the underlying cause is a server response rather than anything visual, so the request and response are given in full below instead — they show the cause where a picture of the dialog could not.

h3. Technical details for developers

The dialog asks for the staff member's hours and is told the staff member does not exist:

{{GET /api/staff/11d2d65b-d8c5-48cf-b34b-382f039d2e12/working-hours}}

{{404  {"errors":[{"error":"'Staff' was not found."}]}}}

The same id, on a neighbouring call made by the same dialog moments earlier, is found without difficulty:

{{GET /api/staff/11d2d65b-d8c5-48cf-b34b-382f039d2e12/enrolled-workplaces}}

{{200  { ... "name":"Staging Lethbridge - 4310" ... }}}

So the record exists and the endpoint can see it; it is the working-hours lookup that appears to be filtered by the session's current workplace. Switching the session with {{POST /api/iam/change-location}} flips the result deterministically and reversibly:

* session on Heavy Duty - 9919: Benjamin Peters {{404}}, Ayesha Khan AK {{200}}
* session on Lethbridge - 4310: Benjamin Peters {{200}}, Ayesha Khan AK {{200}}
* session back on Heavy Duty - 9919: Benjamin Peters {{404}} again

Scope was measured rather than estimated. Every staff record in the list was probed on its {{staff_id}}: *63 of 161 return 404 and 98 return 200*. Technicians are the most affected group (34 of 54).

One note that may save time: this endpoint takes the {{staff_id}} field, which is a different value from the {{id}} field on the same row of the staff list (for Ayesha Khan AK, {{id}} is 24e7590c-7f44-4121-964f-af495c72e2f4 while {{staff_id}} is 1e81b8a0-9a45-4f16-89e3-209bf240990a). Probing with the wrong one returns the same 404 for everybody.

A duplicate search was run before filing. Five queries were used: every descendant of epic SV-8685 (68 issues), and project-wide text searches for "working hours", "custom hours", summary "hours", and "Staff was not found". The nearest reports are all different faults:

* SV-8887, SV-8890, SV-8891 and SV-8892 are all about the hours editor once it is open - minute granularity, overlap colouring, row alignment and end-before-start validation. This report is about the editor never opening.
* SV-8851 is the Tech Hours display switch on the Schedule board.
* SV-8827 is about that switch's default state.
* SV-8831 and SV-8922 are the opposite direction - somebody appearing on the Schedule grid who has no staff record for the location.

items.fromString:
h3. Description

The Schedule can show a unit's VIN on the shift blocks. That is useful in Day and Week view, where a block is wide enough to carry an extra line of text. In Month view the blocks are small, and the specification says the VIN is deliberately left off there so the block stays readable.

Month view shows it anyway. The VIN is printed on the blocks alongside the customer, the unit number and the job, which crowds an already small block and pushes the job description out of sight.

It matters because Month view is the planning view - it is where a service manager looks across four or five weeks at once - and the block text is what makes a job recognisable at a glance. A 17-character VIN takes the space the job description needed.

h3. Branch / Environment

* Application: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com
* API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com
* Build marker ({{<meta name="app-version">}}): {{v3.5-7ec992f}}
* index.html last-modified: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT, etag {{e2a80a6ab5e0b47c29fd88af9db1e980}}
* Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f
* Location / workplace: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton)
* Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator)
* Observed: 2026-08-06, 06:0x UTC

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Sign in as an Administrator on the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and open Schedule from the top navigation.
# Open the *FILTER & DISPLAY* dropdown in the toolbar and turn the *VIN Number* switch *ON*. (It is off by default, so this step is needed - the fault is about what Month view does when the switch is on.)
# Switch to Week view using the Day / Week / Month control and look at the blocks. The VIN appears - this part is correct.
# Now switch to Month view and look at the blocks.
# Switch to Day view and look again - the VIN appears there too, which is also correct.

No special test data is needed beyond a unit that actually has a VIN recorded; the week of 2 to 8 August 2026 on this shop already contains several.

h3. Expected behaviour

Month view blocks should not show the VIN at all, even with the switch on.

Schedule specification, Confluence page 713031682, version 23, section 4.4, states it plainly:

{{"Shown in day and week views only; month view omits it due to space constraints."}}

h3. Current behaviour

With the VIN Number switch on, Month view prints the VIN on the blocks that have one.

* *Month view: 11 of 67* blocks carry a full 17-character VIN.
* Week view: 29 of 55 blocks - *correct*
* Day view: 6 of 12 blocks - *correct*

Examples read straight off the Month view blocks:

* {{Xiriver Apparel ~ 24069 ~ 3HSDZAPT9KN042164 ~ 19 Lines ~ Part of a series}}
* {{Xiriver Apparel ~ 16604 ~ 2H9U7A228VA048027 ~ Service - Wheels off single or tandem axle}}
* {{Pamill Paving ~ 713 ~ 3HAEUMMP1NL291283 ~ Replace - Rear ramp handles}}

Not every block shows one, because not every unit has a VIN recorded - some carry a unit number such as {{12-06696}} instead. The fault is that any VIN appears in Month view at all.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The block text is quoted verbatim above, which shows the VIN more precisely than a picture of a small block would, and the check is a single glance at Month view with the switch on.

h3. Technical details for developers

Counted by reading the rendered top-level block elements ({{.fc-timeline-event}}, {{.fc-daygrid-event}}) in each view and matching their text against a strict VIN pattern - exactly 17 characters from the VIN alphabet, containing at least one digit and at least one letter, so that unit numbers and job codes cannot be mistaken for a VIN.

A first pass used a looser pattern and a selector that also matched nested child elements; it produced inflated and unreliable counts and was discarded. The figures above come from the corrected method, with the raw block text kept alongside each count.

The same switch was confirmed to be doing its job elsewhere in the same sitting, so this is specific to Month view rather than the switch being ignored: with the switch off no block in any view carries a VIN, and with it on both Day and Week views show it as intended.

A duplicate search was run before filing. Four queries were used: every descendant of epic SV-8685 (69 issues), and project-wide text searches for "VIN", summary "VIN", and "month view".

* SV-8835 is the closest and is NOT this: it reports the hover TOOLTIP showing the VIN while the toggle is OFF. This report is about the BLOCK in Month view while the toggle is ON - a different surface and the opposite switch position. (The tooltip behaviour SV-8835 describes was in fact ruled correct by the product owner on 31 July 2026.)
* SV-8865, SV-8867, SV-8870 and SV-8909 are all Month view faults but concern opening, reassigning, drag-creating and empty-cell clicking - none touches block text.

fields.summary: Month view shows the VIN on shift blocks although the spec says it is omitted there

renderedFields.description:
Description

The Schedule can show a unit's VIN on the shift blocks. That is useful in Day and Week view, where a block is wide enough to carry an extra line of text. In Month view the blocks are small, and the specification says the VIN is deliberately left off there so the block stays readable.

Month view shows it anyway. The VIN is printed on the blocks alongside the customer, the unit number and the job, which crowds an already small block and pushes the job description out of sight.

It matters because Month view is the planning view - it is where a service manager looks across four or five weeks at once - and the block text is what makes a job recognisable at a glance. A 17-character VIN takes the space the job description needed.

Branch / Environment

  • Application: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com
  • API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com
  • Build marker (<meta name="app-version">): v3.5-7ec992f
  • index.html last-modified: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT, etag e2a80a6ab5e0b47c29fd88af9db1e980
  • Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f
  • Location / workplace: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton)
  • Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator)
  • Observed: 2026-08-06, 06:0x UTC

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in as an Administrator on the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and open Schedule from the top navigation.
  2. Open the FILTER & DISPLAY dropdown in the toolbar and turn the VIN Number switch ON. (It is off by default, so this step is needed - the fault is about what Month view does when the switch is on.)
  3. Switch to Week view using the Day / Week / Month control and look at the blocks. The VIN appears - this part is correct.
  4. Now switch to Month view and look at the blocks.
  5. Switch to Day view and look again - the VIN appears there too, which is also correct.

No special test data is needed beyond a unit that actually has a VIN recorded; the week of 2 to 8 August 2026 on this shop already contains several.

Expected behaviour

Month view blocks should not show the VIN at all, even with the switch on.

Schedule specification, Confluence page 713031682, version 23, section 4.4, states it plainly:

"Shown in day and week views only; month view omits it due to space constraints."

Current behaviour

With the VIN Number switch on, Month view prints the VIN on the blocks that have one.

  • Month view: 11 of 67 blocks carry a full 17-character VIN.
  • Week view: 29 of 55 blocks - correct
  • Day view: 6 of 12 blocks - correct

Examples read straight off the Month view blocks:

  • Xiriver Apparel ~ 24069 ~ 3HSDZAPT9KN042164 ~ 19 Lines ~ Part of a series
  • Xiriver Apparel ~ 16604 ~ 2H9U7A228VA048027 ~ Service - Wheels off single or tandem axle
  • Pamill Paving ~ 713 ~ 3HAEUMMP1NL291283 ~ Replace - Rear ramp handles

Not every block shows one, because not every unit has a VIN recorded - some carry a unit number such as 12-06696 instead. The fault is that any VIN appears in Month view at all.

Images

No screenshot is attached. The block text is quoted verbatim above, which shows the VIN more precisely than a picture of a small block would, and the check is a single glance at Month view with the switch on.

Technical details for developers

Counted by reading the rendered top-level block elements (.fc-timeline-event, .fc-daygrid-event) in each view and matching their text against a strict VIN pattern - exactly 17 characters from the VIN alphabet, containing at least one digit and at least one letter, so that unit numbers and job codes cannot be mistaken for a VIN.

A first pass used a looser pattern and a selector that also matched nested child elements; it produced inflated and unreliable counts and was discarded. The figures above come from the corrected method, with the raw block text kept alongside each count.

The same switch was confirmed to be doing its job elsewhere in the same sitting, so this is specific to Month view rather than the switch being ignored: with the switch off no block in any view carries a VIN, and with it on both Day and Week views show it as intended.

A duplicate search was run before filing. Four queries were used: every descendant of epic SV-8685 Open (69 issues), and project-wide text searches for "VIN", summary "VIN", and "month view".

  • SV-8835 Ready to Fix is the closest and is NOT this: it reports the hover TOOLTIP showing the VIN while the toggle is OFF. This report is about the BLOCK in Month view while the toggle is ON - a different surface and the opposite switch position. (The tooltip behaviour SV-8835 Ready to Fix describes was in fact ruled correct by the product owner on 31 July 2026.)
  • SV-8865 Ready for QA , SV-8867 In Progress , SV-8870 OBSOLETE and SV-8909 OBSOLETE are all Month view faults but concern opening, reassigning, drag-creating and empty-cell clicking - none touches block text.
