Shown in day and week views only; month view omits it due to space constraints."

items.fromString:
h3. What happens now

The Schedule page is meant to cope with a narrow screen by letting the *grid* slide sideways while the left-hand panel folds away. Neither happens. Make the browser window narrower and the *whole page* starts sliding sideways instead - the top navigation, the toolbar and everything else go with it - while the left-hand work order panel stays exactly as wide as it was.

h3. Why this matters

A planner on a laptop or a small window ends up scrolling the entire page left and right just to see the end of the week, and the panel that should have got out of the way is still taking up a third of the screen. Nothing is lost or broken, but the page becomes awkward to work in.

h3. How to see it

# Sign in and open the Schedule page in Week view.
# Make the browser window 960 pixels wide - that is the narrowest width the Schedule is supposed to support.
# Look at the left-hand work order panel, and try scrolling the page sideways.
# Narrow it further, to 900 and then to 700 pixels, and look again.

h3. What you see

* The left-hand panel keeps the same width the whole way down - 275 pixels of content inside a 299 pixel column - at 1000, 960, 900 and 700 pixels alike. It never folds away.
* The page itself is what scrolls sideways. Its total width stays stuck at 1030 pixels no matter how narrow the window gets, so the sideways scrollbar belongs to the whole page and not to the grid.
* There is no sideways scroller on the grid at all. The only things that overflow are the page and its outer containers.
* At a full 1680 pixel window there is no sideways scrolling at all, so this only appears once the window is narrowed.

h3. What should happen

From the Schedule specification, section 11: *"Minimum supported width is 960px (the grid scrolls horizontally below that), and the sidebar collapses on narrow viewports."*

* The grid - not the page - should be the thing that scrolls sideways.
* The left-hand panel should collapse once the window is narrow.

h3. Exact test data used

* Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
* Schedule page, Week view, the week of 3 August 2026, with 22 technician rows and 55 shift blocks showing.
* Signed in as admin@shopview.com.
* Widths measured: 1680, 1000, 960, 900 and 700 pixels, window height 1000.

h3. Things checked and ruled out first

* Not a stray error - the page reports zero errors at every width tested.
* Not only a below-minimum problem. It happens at exactly 960 pixels, which the specification calls the narrowest supported width, so it is inside the supported range and not just an edge case.
* Not a missed element - every element on the page that overflows was listed, and the only ones are the page itself and its outer containers. No grid-level scroller exists to have been missed.
* Not the full-size layout - at 1680 pixels the page width matches the window exactly.

h3. Where this came from

Found while running the Schedule test case {{SCH-EDGE-01}} (TestRail C30086) against build {{v3.5-7ec992f}} on 6 August 2026.

items.fromString:
h3. What happens now

The only way to put a job on the Schedule is to drag it. There used to be a click alternative - you clicked a small control on the work order card, the card showed as armed, and you then clicked the technician's cell to place the job. That control has gone from the current build, so anyone who cannot drag has no way to schedule at all.

h3. Why this matters

Dragging is hard or impossible for some people - anyone using a keyboard, a trackpad they struggle with, or assistive software. The Schedule specification asks for a click alternative precisely so that scheduling does not depend on being able to drag. With it gone, the whole feature is unreachable for those users.

h3. How to see it

# Sign in and open the Schedule page.
# Look at any work order card in the left-hand panel. Hover over it.
# Open the card's line list too, using the arrow on the right.
# Look for any button that arms the card for click placement.

h3. What you see

* There is no such button anywhere - not on the card, not when hovering it, and not inside the line list.
* The card carries no button of any kind. Its only interactive parts are the status chip and the arrow that opens the line list.
* It was there in an earlier build of this same branch, where the control was labelled so that it read as "Schedule S-12876 by click", and clicking it turned the card on and then let a technician cell be clicked to place the job.

h3. What should happen

From the Schedule specification, section 11: *"drag-and-drop has a click-to-arm alternative".* The click alternative should be present and should place a job on the cell you click, opening the same scope window the drag opens.

h3. Exact test data used

* Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Build v3.5-7ec992f (index.html last modified Wed 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT).
* Work order card S-12876, Pamill Paving, unit 713, 1 line, and also a multi-line card S-13014, Fuline Enterprises, unit G30, 7 lines.
* Signed in as admin@shopview.com, week of 3 August 2026, Week view.
* The control it replaced was seen on the earlier build v3.5-be42149 of this same branch.

h3. Things checked and ruled out first

* Not hidden until hover - hovering the card was tried and adds nothing.
* Not tucked inside the line list - the list was opened and its controls are only a back button, a search box, two scope buttons and the line rows.
* Not a naming change - the whole page was searched for any control whose test name or accessible label mentions arming or clicking to schedule, and there are none.
* Not a permissions problem - this was seen as an administrator with the full Schedule permission.
* This is separate from the drag problems already reported. SV-8840 and SV-8869 are about missing drag feedback, SV-8870 is about Month view, and SV-8867 is about reassigning a series. None of them is about the click alternative being absent.

h3. Where this came from

Found while re-checking the Schedule test cases {{SCH-DND-08}} (TestRail C29962) and {{SCH-SCOPE-05}} (TestRail C29967) against build {{v3.5-7ec992f}} on 6 August 2026. C29962 was recorded as passing on the earlier build of this branch, which is how the change was noticed.

fields.summary: Schedule: the click alternative to dragging a job onto the grid has disappeared from the build

comments.body: Branko Cicovic Milos Vasic - take a look at this one. Branko and I discussed this already, and agreed this functionality should not be in the scope of v1.

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

The only way to put a job on the Schedule is to drag it. There used to be a click alternative - you clicked a small control on the work order card, the card showed as armed, and you then clicked the technician's cell to place the job. That control has gone from the current build, so anyone who cannot drag has no way to schedule at all.

Why this matters

Dragging is hard or impossible for some people - anyone using a keyboard, a trackpad they struggle with, or assistive software. The Schedule specification asks for a click alternative precisely so that scheduling does not depend on being able to drag. With it gone, the whole feature is unreachable for those users.

How to see it

  1. Sign in and open the Schedule page.
  2. Look at any work order card in the left-hand panel. Hover over it.
  3. Open the card's line list too, using the arrow on the right.
  4. Look for any button that arms the card for click placement.

What you see

  • There is no such button anywhere - not on the card, not when hovering it, and not inside the line list.
  • The card carries no button of any kind. Its only interactive parts are the status chip and the arrow that opens the line list.
  • It was there in an earlier build of this same branch, where the control was labelled so that it read as "Schedule S-12876 by click", and clicking it turned the card on and then let a technician cell be clicked to place the job.

What should happen

From the Schedule specification, section 11: "drag-and-drop has a click-to-arm alternative". The click alternative should be present and should place a job on the cell you click, opening the same scope window the drag opens.

Exact test data used

  • Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Build v3.5-7ec992f (index.html last modified Wed 05 Aug 2026 22:49:36 GMT).
  • Work order card S-12876, Pamill Paving, unit 713, 1 line, and also a multi-line card S-13014, Fuline Enterprises, unit G30, 7 lines.
  • Signed in as admin@shopview.com, week of 3 August 2026, Week view.
  • The control it replaced was seen on the earlier build v3.5-be42149 of this same branch.

Things checked and ruled out first

  • Not hidden until hover - hovering the card was tried and adds nothing.
  • Not tucked inside the line list - the list was opened and its controls are only a back button, a search box, two scope buttons and the line rows.
  • Not a naming change - the whole page was searched for any control whose test name or accessible label mentions arming or clicking to schedule, and there are none.
  • Not a permissions problem - this was seen as an administrator with the full Schedule permission.
  • This is separate from the drag problems already reported. SV-8840 Ready for QA and SV-8869 Ready for QA are about missing drag feedback, SV-8870 OBSOLETE is about Month view, and SV-8867 In Progress is about reassigning a series. None of them is about the click alternative being absent.

Where this came from

Found while re-checking the Schedule test cases SCH-DND-08 (TestRail C29962) and SCH-SCOPE-05 (TestRail C29967) against build v3.5-7ec992f on 6 August 2026. C29962 was recorded as passing on the earlier build of this branch, which is how the change was noticed.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Schedule specification, version 23, section 11 (Non-functional requirements), which says under Accessibility: "drag-and-drop has a click-to-arm alternative". The same specification repeats it in section 7 (Interactions and micro-interactions): "Drag-and-drop has a click-to-arm alternative for users who cannot drag."

items.fromString:
h3. What happens now

In Month view a job spread over several days is drawn as one bar, but the bar does not say whose it is. It shows the customer, the unit, how many lines the job has and the words "Part of a series" - and no technician name anywhere.

h3. Why this matters

Month view has no technician rows to read the name off, unlike Day and Week. So a planner looking at the month cannot tell who a job is booked to without opening it.

h3. How to see it

# Open the Schedule page and switch to Month view.
# Find a job that runs over several days - it will say "Part of a series".
# Read the bar from left to right.

h3. What you see

* The bar reads, for example, "Xiriver Apparel  24069  19 Lines  Part of a series" and another reads "Kastone Solutions  HE2-001  7 Lines  Part of a series".
* No technician name or initials appear on the bar at all.

h3. What should happen

From the Schedule specification, section 4.6: *"Month view: a continuous bar wrapping across week rows, labeled once at the start (with the technician)".* The label at the start of the bar should include the technician.

h3. Exact test data used

* Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Build v3.5-7ec992f. Signed in as admin@shopview.com.
* Month view covering August 2026. Series bars seen: Xiriver Apparel unit 24069 (19 lines) and Kastone Solutions unit HE2-001 (7 lines).
* Six series entries were read in Month view; none carried a technician.

h3. Things checked and ruled out first

* Not a display setting - the VIN switch and the department filters were not the cause; the technician is simply not part of the bar's text.
* Not a Week-view problem - in Week view the technician is the row, so the name is available there. This is specific to Month view.
* Not the same as the missing chevrons and week counter reported in SV-8895; those were checked on this build and the chevron and the "Week 1 of 2" text are present.

h3. Where this came from

Found while re-checking Schedule test case {{SCH-SER-01}} (TestRail C29987) on 6 August 2026.

items.fromString:
h3. What happens now

When you hover a shift that has a clash, the tooltip does warn you - but the warning sits at the very bottom of the tooltip, several rows below the customer name. The customer name row itself carries no warning mark.

h3. Why this matters

The customer name is the first thing anyone reads. Putting the warning at the bottom means a planner scanning quickly can miss that the shift has a clash at all.

h3. How to see it

# Open the Schedule page in Week view.
# Find a shift that shows an amber warning triangle on the block itself.
# Hover over the middle of that block and wait for the tooltip.
# Read the tooltip from the top down.

h3. What you see

* The first row is just the customer name - for example "Brabay Maintenance" - with no warning mark next to it.
* The warning appears only in the last row, as "Starts before working hours - Extends past working hours - Double-booked" with a triangle beside it.
* The warning text is amber, which is correct.

h3. What should happen

From the Schedule specification, section 4.13, the shift tooltip's first line is *"customer name (plus the conflict icon if conflicted)".* The warning mark belongs next to the customer name.

h3. Exact test data used

* Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Build v3.5-7ec992f. Signed in as admin@shopview.com.
* The shift hovered: Brabay Maintenance, VIN C44ECN300699, Tuesday 4 August 2026, 27 lines, technician Ayesha Khan AK, three clash reasons at once.
* Week of 3 August 2026, Week view, at a 1680 by 1050 window.

h3. Things checked and ruled out first

* Not a missing tooltip - the whole tooltip renders correctly, with customer, VIN, date and time, technician, line list and progress bar.
* Not the amber colour - the reason text is amber as the specification asks, so only the position of the mark is wrong.
* Not the wrong tooltip - the shift's own tooltip was read, not the small tooltip that the warning triangle on the block shows on its own.
* Not the same as SV-8877, which is about the conflict LIST not naming the technician or day. This is the hover tooltip's layout.

h3. Where this came from

Found while re-checking Schedule test case {{SCH-TIP-02}} (TestRail C30035) on 6 August 2026.
